\parbox{\columnwidth}{\scriptsize Batch size 1, test frames in time order, RTX 3090 and AMD EPYC 7452, PyTorch 2.4.1, one session on a host shared with other tenants (1-min load average 56--130 before the runs; GPU idle). (a) 20 warm-up frames, then 3$\times$100 timed frames; percentiles over the 300 frames. Objects: mean and maximum number of objects per timed frame. $\rho$: Spearman correlation between the latency and the number of objects of a frame. TensorRT: FP16 engines for the two YOLO11n models, the image encoder in PyTorch, as in Table~\ref{tab:speed}; PyTorch: all networks in PyTorch. Avenue in this session versus Table~\ref{tab:speed} (another session and host): see the text. $^{c}$Development set. (b) \texttt{tools/bench\_pipeline.py}: DIS flow, autoencoder, cell statistics, tail calibration, fusion and causal median, without the object branch; 3$\times$100 timed frames after 5 warm-up frames each, median over the three repetitions of the per-repetition median and 95th percentile; frame size (width$\times$height) as processed by the grid branch (Section~\ref{sec:grid}). This is not the latency of the object + grid configuration: the two branches are not combined in one streaming implementation. (c) As (a), in a third session on an RTX 3090 with an AMD Ryzen 9 7945HX CPU (1-min load average at most 4.2), with the configurations of Table~\ref{tab:main} with and without the pose model, alternating; objects per frame as in (a); saved: difference of the p50 values. The GPU was not idle: before 13 of the 18 measurements (fits included) nvidia-smi reported 37--100\% utilisation with no process listed, and a display was attached. The absolute values are therefore not comparable with (a).}
